'''Kristopher Nathan Humphries'''<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/hawks/features/kris-humphries-beat-michael-phelps-and-ryan-lochte-swimming-kid-and-heres-proof/|title=Kris Humphries Beat Michael Phelps and Ryan Lochte At Swimming As A Kid, And Here's Proof|work=NBA.com|date=August 15, 2016|access-date=August 17, 2016}}</ref> (born February 6, 1985) is an American former professional [[basketball]] [[power forward]] who played in the [[National Basketball Association]] (NBA). He played in the NBA for the [[Utah Jazz]], [[Toronto Raptors]], [[Dallas Mavericks]], [[Brooklyn Nets|New Jersey / Brooklyn Nets]], [[Boston Celtics]], [[Washington Wizards]], [[Phoenix Suns]], and the [[Atlanta Hawks]] from 2004 to 2016. Humphries played [[college basketball]] for the [[Minnesota Golden Gophers men's basketball|Minnesota Golden Gophers]] and for the [[United States men's national basketball team]]. He was married to [[Kim Kardashian]] for 72 days before they divorced.

==Early life==
Humphries was born in [[Minnesota]] to Debra and William Humphries. His father was a [[American football|football]] player at the [[University of Minnesota]].<ref name=usa>{{cite web|title=USA Basketball Bio: Kris Humphries |url=http://www.usabasketball.com/biosmen/kris_humphries_bio.html |work=USABasketball.com |access-date=April 29, 2007 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20060327043119/http://www.usabasketball.com/biosmen/kris_humphries_bio.html |archive-date=March 27, 2006 }}</ref> Humphries is half-[[African Americans|African American]] from his father.<ref>{{cite web|title=Kim Kardashian & Kris Humphries To Wed This Summer! Wedding Could Net Over $5 Million|url=http://www.realitytea.com/tag/kris-humphries-race/|work=RealityTea.com|date=May 27, 2011|access-date=May 27, 2011}}</ref> He has two older sisters, Krystal and Kaela. His first success in sports came in competitive swimming, where he was the top 10-year-old in the nation in six events, first, beating young [[Michael Phelps]] in the remaining events. Kris Humphries held the US national record for the 50-meter freestyle for 10 and under boys for 18 years until it was recently broken.<ref>{{cite web|title=USA Swimming National Age Group Records|url=http://usaswimming.org/_Rainbow/Documents/e8f10a43-499e-4c61-a6e3-3d6abe76f29d/USA%20SWIMMING%20NATIONAL%20A%20G%20%20RECORDS%20L%20C.pdf|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20131105014941/http://www.usaswimming.org/_Rainbow/Documents/e8f10a43-499e-4c61-a6e3-3d6abe76f29d/USA%20SWIMMING%20NATIONAL%20A%20G%20%20RECORDS%20L%20C.pdf|url-status=dead|archive-date=November 5, 2013|work=USASwimming.org|access-date=January 4, 2014}}</ref> At age 12, he gave up swimming to pursue a career in basketball.

Humphries attended [[Hopkins High School]], where he led the team to a 25–2 record in 2002 and its first Minnesota state championship in 49 years.<ref name=usa/> He was named a 2003 [[McDonald's All-American Team|McDonald's All-American]] and named Second Team All-USA by [[USA Today]].<ref name=bio>{{cite web|title=Kris Humphries Info Page – Bio|url=http://www.nba.com/playerfile/kris_humphries/bio/|work=NBA.com|access-date=April 14, 2007|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140306120916/http://www.nba.com/playerfile/kris_humphries/bio/|archive-date=March 6, 2014}}</ref> He was also named to the Super 25 Basketball Team by USA Today, named [[Minnesota Mr. Basketball]], and state player of the year by the [[Minneapolis Star Tribune]] and College Basketball News.<ref name=bio/> He was one of 10 finalists for the 2003 Naismith Prep Player of the Year Award, averaging a [[double-double]] in his final three seasons, averaging 25.7 [[point (basketball)|points]], 11.4 [[rebound (basketball)|rebounds]], and 5.0 [[assist (basketball)|assists]] a game as a senior.<ref name=bio/>

Considered a five-star recruit by [[Rivals.com]], Humphries was listed as the No. 2 power forward and the No. 15 player in the nation in 2003.<ref>{{cite web|title=Kris Humphries Recruiting Profile|url=https://n.rivals.com/content/prospects/maple/4700|work=Rivals.com|access-date=January 6, 2012}}</ref>

Humphries accepted a scholarship offer to [[Duke University]], but later reconsidered and chose the [[University of Minnesota]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Duke releases McDonald's recruit Kris Humphries|url=http://usatoday30.usatoday.com/sports/college/mensbasketball/acc/2003-05-19-duke-humphries_x.htm|work=USA Today|date=May 19, 2003|access-date=January 6, 2012}}</ref>

==College career==
At Minnesota, Humphries was named 2004 [[Big Ten Conference|Big Ten]] Freshman of the Year and named to the All-Big Ten First Team by the media and coaches. He was named Honorable Mention All-America by the [[Associated Press]] and by Rivals.com. He was the first freshman to lead the Big Ten in scoring and rebounding in the same season. He scored in double figures in all the 29 games, with 16 point/rebound double-doubles on the season for Minnesota. He averaged 21.7 points and 10.1 rebounds (both tops in the Big Ten), while shooting .444 [[field goal percentage|percent from the field]] and .742 [[free throw|from the line]]. On February 18, 2004, he set a school record with 36 points in a game against [[Indiana University Bloomington|Indiana]]. He also set a school record for most points by a freshman for a season with 629 and was the first Big Ten freshman to be named conference Player of the Week in two of the first three weeks of the season. Humphries only played one season for Minnesota before declaring for the [[NBA draft]].

Although Humphries was personally successful at Minnesota, the team struggled. The Gophers finished 12–18, with a 3–13 record in the Big Ten during Humphries' lone season, tying Penn State for the worst record in the conference.<ref>{{cite web|title=NCAA Division I Basketball Standings – 2003–04|url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/standings/_/year/2004|work=ESPN.com|access-date=January 6, 2012}}</ref> Critics accused Humphries of playing selfishly, preferring to inflate his statistics and NBA draft stock rather than help the team win games.<ref>{{cite web|first=Michael |last=Rand |title=Top recruits have had problems at U |url=http://www.startribune.com/sports/gophers/83305812.html?page=2&c=y |work=StarTribune.com |date=February 10, 2010 |access-date=February 10, 2010 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100210225938/http://www.startribune.com/sports/gophers/83305812.html?page=2&c=y |archive-date=February 10, 2010 }}</ref> The team had a .500 record before his arrival and finished with a 10–6 conference record in the season after he left. At the 2004 NBA Combine, Humphries benched an impressive 22 reps of 185 pounds.

==Professional career==

===Utah Jazz (2004–2006)===
Humphries was [[NBA draft|drafted]] by the [[Utah Jazz]] with the 14th overall selection in the [[2004 NBA draft]].<ref>{{cite web|title=HUMPHRIES TAKEN BY UTAH WITH 14TH PICK OF NBA DRAFT|url=http://www.gophersports.com/sports/m-baskbl/spec-rel/062504aaa.html|work=GopherSports.com|date=June 25, 2004|access-date=March 5, 2016|archive-date=September 10, 2015|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150910030448/http://www.gophersports.com/sports/m-baskbl/spec-rel/062504aaa.html|url-status=dead}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|title=Kris Humphries Statistics|url=https://www.basketball-reference.com/players/h/humphkr01.html|work=Basketball-Reference.com|access-date=April 29, 2007}}</ref> He spent two seasons with the Jazz, averaging 3.7 ppg and 2.8 rpg in 4.8 minutes per game.<ref name=stats>{{cite web|title=Kris Humphries Info Page – Career Stats and Totals|url=http://www.nba.com/playerfile/kris_humphries/|work=NBA.com|access-date=April 29, 2007}}</ref>

===Toronto Raptors (2006–2009)===
On June 8, 2006, Humphries was traded along with [[Robert Whaley]] to the [[Toronto Raptors]] in exchange for [[Rafael Paulo de Lara Araújo|Rafael Araújo]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Raptors Acquire Kris Humphries & Robert Whaley for Araujo|url=http://www.nba.com/raptors/news/pressrelease_trade_060806.html|work=NBA.com|date=June 8, 2006|access-date=April 29, 2007}}</ref> In the [[2006–07 NBA Season|2006–07 season]], after a slow start in which he did not receive many minutes from Raptors coach [[Sam Mitchell (basketball)|Sam Mitchell]], Humphries proved to be a valuable rebounder and energy player and contributed to the Raptors capturing their first ever [[Atlantic Division (NBA)|division]] title.<ref>{{cite web|first=Morgan|last=Campbell|title=Humphries, Jackson bring energy off Raptors' bench|url=https://www.thestar.com/news/2007/04/15/humphries_jackson_bring_energy_off_raptors_bench.html|work=TheStar.com|date=April 15, 2007|access-date=April 15, 2007}}</ref> On March 28, 2007, he grabbed seven offensive rebounds in 27 minutes against the [[Miami Heat]], both a game-high<ref>{{cite web|title=Raptors Burn Heat, Grab Control of Third Place in East|url=http://www.nba.com/games/20070328/MIATOR/recap.html|work=NBA.com|date=March 28, 2007|access-date=April 14, 2007}}</ref> and a career-high.<ref>{{cite web|first=Bruce |last=Arthur |title=Small Raptors come up big against Heat |url=http://www2.canada.com/topics/sports/basketball/raptorsstory.html?id=c0bca271-f678-41a2-9412-7a894ad63bbc&k=54662 |publisher=Canada.com |date=March 29, 2007 |access-date=April 29, 2007 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140716175908/http://www2.canada.com/topics/sports/basketball/raptorsstory.html?id=c0bca271-f678-41a2-9412-7a894ad63bbc&k=54662 |archive-date=July 16, 2014 }}</ref> He followed up this performance with nine offensive and 18 total rebounds in a win against the [[Detroit Pistons]] on April 13, 2007, again both game and career-highs.<ref>{{cite web|title=Parker, Raptors Rally Past Pistons|url=http://www.nba.com/games/20070413/DETTOR/recap.html|work=NBA.com|date=April 13, 2007|access-date=April 14, 2007}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|title=Raptors Post Up |url=http://www.nba.com/raptors/news/postup_041307.html |work=NBA.com |date=April 13, 2007 |access-date=April 13, 2007 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20070618183728/http://www.nba.com/raptors/news/postup_041307.html |archive-date=June 18, 2007 }}</ref> Humphries concluded his inaugural season with the Raptors with a career-high 3.1 rpg and .470 [[field goal percentage]], as well as 3.8 ppg.<ref name=stats/>

===Dallas Mavericks (2009–2010)===
[[File:Kris Humphries.jpg|thumb|right|130px|Humphries played with the [[Dallas Mavericks]] during the {{nbay|2009}} season.]]
On July 9, 2009, Humphries, [[Shawn Marion]] and [[Nathan Jawai]] were traded to the [[Dallas Mavericks]] as a part of the four-team deal among Raptors, Mavericks, [[Orlando Magic]] and [[Memphis Grizzlies]].<ref>{{cite web|title=MAVERICKS ACQUIRE FOUR-TIME ALL-STAR SHAWN MARION |url=http://www.nba.com/mavericks/roster/shawnmarion.html |work=NBA.com |date=July 9, 2009 |access-date=July 9, 2009 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130814132558/http://www.nba.com/mavericks/roster/shawnmarion.html |archive-date=August 14, 2013 }}</ref>

===New Jersey / Brooklyn Nets (2010–2013)===
On January 11, 2010, the Mavericks traded Humphries along with G/F [[Shawne Williams]] to the [[New Jersey Nets]] in order to re-acquire [[Eduardo Nájera]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Nets Acquire Kris Humphries and Shawne Williams from Dallas|url=http://www.nba.com/nets/news/Najera_Humphries_Trade_Release_100111.html|work=NBA.com|date=January 11, 2010|access-date =January 12, 2010}}</ref> On January 27, 2010, Humphries scored a career-high 25 points against the Los Angeles Clippers. He previously recorded career highs of 15 and 21 points respectively as a New Jersey Net.{{Citation needed|date=August 2011}} The 2011 season was a breakout season for Humphries as he averaged a double-double in points and rebounds. On December 21, 2011, Humphries signed a one-year, $8 million contract with the [[New Jersey Nets]].<ref>{{cite web|title=NETS Re-Sign Kris Humphries|url=http://www.nba.com/nets/news/Humphries_Resigns_Release_111221.html|work=NBA.com|date=December 21, 2011|access-date=December 21, 2011}}</ref>

The 2011–12 season was his best as a professional, as he started all 62 games that he played in, averaging 13.8 points, 11.0 rebounds, and 1.2 blocked shots per game – all career highs. His rebounding average was good enough to rank fifth in the league for the second consecutive season.

On July 17, 2012, Humphries signed a two-year, $24 million contract with the Nets, who by that point had moved to [[Brooklyn]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Brooklyn Nets Agree to Re-Sign Kris Humphries|url=http://www.nba.com/nets/news/Humphries_Signing_Release_120717.html|work=NBA.com|date=July 17, 2012|access-date=July 17, 2012}}</ref>

===Boston Celtics (2013–2014)===
On June 27, 2013, [[ESPN.com]] reported that the Nets and [[Boston Celtics]] had worked out a trade that would send Humphries and four other players ([[Keith Bogans]], [[MarShon Brooks]], [[Kris Joseph]], and [[Gerald Wallace]]) as well as three future first-round [[National Basketball Association draft|draft]] picks to Boston in exchange for [[Kevin Garnett]], [[Paul Pierce]], and [[Jason Terry]] as well as [[D. J. White]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Nets, Celtics work out blockbuster|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/story/_/id/9429958/sources-boston-celtics-brooklyn-nets-agree-kevin-garnett-paul-pierce-deal|work=ESPN.com|date=June 27, 2013|access-date=June 28, 2013}}</ref> The deal was finally completed on July 12, 2013.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/nets/news/nets-acquire-nba-champions-kevin-garnett-paul-pierce-and-jason-terry|title=Nets Acquire NBA Champions Kevin Garnett, Paul Pierce and Jason Terry|work=NBA.com|date=July 12, 2013|access-date=July 12, 2013}}</ref>

===Washington Wizards (2014–2016)===
On July 19, 2014, Humphries was acquired by the [[Washington Wizards]] in a sign-and-trade deal that sent a protected 2015 second round pick and a trade exception to the Boston Celtics.<ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.nba.com/celtics/news/pressrelease/celtics-complete-trade-wizards|title=Celtics Complete Trade with Wizards|work=NBA.com|date=July 19, 2014|access-date=July 19, 2014}}</ref> On October 9, 2014, he underwent successful surgery to repair nerve damage in his right small finger, and was subsequently sidelined for three to four weeks.<ref>{{cite news|url=http://wizardsmysticstoday.monumentalnetwork.com/2014/10/10/wizards-injury-update|title=WIZARDS INJURY UPDATE|work=WizardsMysticsToday.MonumentalNetwork.com|date=October 10, 2015|access-date=October 10, 2015}}</ref>

[[File:1 kris humphries 2015.jpg|left|upright|thumb|Humphries with the [[Washington Wizards]] in 2015]]
On November 14, 2015, Humphries made 5-of-8 three-pointers on his way to a game-high 23 points, helping the Wizards defeat the Orlando Magic 108–99. Prior to the 2015–16 season, Humphries had gone more than a decade since making a three-pointer. He hit two in his 2004–05 rookie season, and none after that, until this game.<ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.nba.com/games/20151114/ORLWAS/gameinfo.html|title=Wizards beat Magic 108–99 to end 3-game skid|work=NBA.com|date=November 14, 2015|access-date=November 14, 2015}}</ref>

===Phoenix Suns (2016)===
On February 18, 2016, Humphries was traded, along with [[DeJuan Blair]] and a 2016 protected first round draft pick, to the [[Phoenix Suns]] in exchange for [[Markieff Morris]].<ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.nba.com/suns/suns-trade-morris-first-round-pick|title=Suns Acquire First-Round Pick, Blair, Humphries from Washington for Morris|work=NBA.com|date=February 18, 2016|access-date=February 18, 2016}}</ref> He made his debut for the Suns the following day in a 116–100 loss to the [[Houston Rockets]], recording 18 points and 12 rebounds in 27 minutes off the bench, becoming the 13th Suns player to have a double-double in his debut.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/games/20160219/HOUPHX/gameinfo.html|title=James Harden leads Rockets past free-falling Suns, 116–100|work=NBA.com|publisher=Turner Sports Interactive, Inc.|date=February 19, 2016|access-date=February 20, 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160221004700/http://www.nba.com/games/20160219/HOUPHX/gameinfo.html|archive-date=February 21, 2016|url-status=dead}}</ref> On February 28, after three starts in four games, he was waived by the Suns in a buyout agreement.<ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.nba.com/suns/suns-waive-humphries|title=Suns Waive Humphries|work=NBA.com|date=February 28, 2016|access-date=February 28, 2016}}</ref>

===Atlanta Hawks (2016–2017)===
On March 1, 2016, Humphries signed with the [[Atlanta Hawks]].<ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.nba.com/hawks/news/hawks-sign-kris-humphries|title=Hawks Sign Kris Humphries|work=NBA.com|date=March 1, 2016|access-date=March 1, 2016}}</ref> Three days later, he made his debut for the Hawks in a 106–77 win over the [[Los Angeles Lakers]], recording 14 points, eight rebounds, one steal and one block in 22 minutes off the bench.<ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.nba.com/games/20160304/ATLLAL/gameinfo.html|title=Hawks get balanced scoring in trampling Lakers 106–77|work=NBA.com|date=March 5, 2016|access-date=March 5, 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160306100613/http://www.nba.com/games/20160304/ATLLAL/gameinfo.html|archive-date=March 6, 2016|url-status=dead}}</ref>

On July 15, 2016, Humphries re-signed with the Hawks.<ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.nba.com/hawks/features/hawks-re-sign-humphries-add-jack-delaney|title=Hawks Re-Sign Humphries, Add Jack & Delaney|work=NBA.com|date=July 15, 2016|access-date=July 15, 2016}}</ref>

===Retirement===
On September 25, 2017, Humphries signed with the [[Philadelphia 76ers]]<ref>{{cite web|title=Sixers Sign Humphries, Okafor; Set Training Camp Roster|url=http://www.nba.com/sixers/news/sixers-sign-humphries-okafor-set-training-camp-roster|website=NBA.com|access-date=September 25, 2017|date=September 25, 2017}}</ref> but was waived on October 14, 2017, as one of the final roster cuts.<ref>{{cite web|title=Sixers Waive Three Players|url=http://www.nba.com/sixers/news/sixers-waive-three-players|website=NBA.com|access-date=October 14, 2017|date=October 14, 2017}}</ref> Humphries announced his retirement on March 26, 2019.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Humphries |first1=Kris |title=I Never Wanted to Be That Guy |url=https://www.theplayerstribune.com/articles/kris-humphries-i-never-wanted-to-be-that-guy|website=The Players' Tribune |access-date=March 27, 2019 |date=March 26, 2019}}</ref>

==National team career==
Humphries was on the 2002 U.S. Junior World Championship Qualifying Tournament Team, alongside future Raptors teammate [[Chris Bosh]].<ref name=bio/> The team finished with a 4–1 record and the bronze medal and qualified for a berth in the 2003 FIBA Junior World Championship.<ref name=usa/> Humphries averaged 9.0 points and 5.0 rebounds in five games.<ref name=usa/>

==Personal life==
Humphries began dating reality TV personality [[Kim Kardashian]] in October 2010. They became engaged in May 2011,<ref>{{cite news|first=Jocelyn|last=Vena|url=http://www.mtv.com/news/articles/1673479/kim-kardashian-kris-humphries-timeline.jhtml|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20111102143531/http://www.mtv.com/news/articles/1673479/kim-kardashian-kris-humphries-timeline.jhtml|url-status=dead|archive-date=November 2, 2011|title=Kim Kardashian And Kris Humphries: A Timeline|work=MTV.com|date=October 31, 2011|access-date=October 31, 2011}}</ref> and married on August 20, 2011.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://khitschicago.radio.com/2011/05/25/kardashian-engaged/|title=Kim Kardashian Is Engaged|date=May 25, 2011|work=KHitsChicago.Radio.com|access-date=May 25, 2011|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110529130137/http://khitschicago.radio.com/2011/05/25/kardashian-engaged/|archive-date=May 29, 2011}}</ref> A two-part TV special showing the preparations and the wedding itself aired on [[E!]] in early October 2011, amidst what ''[[The Washington Post]]'' called a "media blitz" related to the wedding.<ref>{{cite news|first=Sarah Anne|last=Hughes|url=https://www.washingtonpost.com/blogs/celebritology/post/kim-kardashian-wedding-special-to-air-this-sunday-will-you-watch-video/2011/10/07/gIQATLFQTL_blog.html|title=Kim Kardashian wedding special to air this Sunday: Will you watch?|date=October 7, 2011|access-date=December 2, 2011|newspaper=The Washington Post}}</ref>

On October 31, 2011, it was announced that Kardashian had filed for divorce from Humphries after 72 days of marriage.<ref>{{cite web|first=Justin|last=Harp|title=Updated: Kim Kardashian files for divorce from Kris Humphries|url=http://www.digitalspy.com/celebrity/news/a348420/kim-kardashian-filing-for-divorce-from-kris-humphries-today.html|work=DigitalSpy.com|publisher=[[Hearst Magazines UK]]|date=October 31, 2011|access-date=October 31, 2011}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|title=The Kim Kardashian And Kris Humphries Marriage Is Over!|url=http://us99country.radio.com/2011/10/31/apparently-the-kim-kardashian-and-kris-humphries-marriage-is-over/|work=WUSN-FM/US99.5|date=October 31, 2011|access-date=October 31, 2011|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120309131310/http://us99country.radio.com/2011/10/31/apparently-the-kim-kardashian-and-kris-humphries-marriage-is-over/|archive-date=March 9, 2012|url-status=dead}}</ref>

On December 1, 2011, Humphries filed his response to Kardashian's petition, requesting an annulment on the grounds of fraud or a decree of legal separation rather than the Kardashian-requested divorce.<ref>{{cite news|title=Kris Humphries' Annulment Filing: Read It Here Now!|url=http://www.eonline.com/ca/news/277969/kris-humphries-annulment-filing-read-it-here-now|publisher=EOnline.com|date=December 1, 2011|access-date=December 2, 2011}}</ref>

Several media outlets at that time reported that Kardashian's marriage to Humphries was a publicity stunt orchestrated by E! Entertainment, [[Kris Jenner]], and Kim Kardashian to promote the [[Kardashian family]]'s brand and their subsequent television ventures; however, there was never any substantial evidence to support that claim.<ref>{{cite news|title=Was Kardashian marriage a sham? |url=http://www.chicagotribune.com/video/breaking/chi-video-was-kim-kardashian-marriage-divorce-a-sham-20111101,0,7143953.htmlstory |work=Chicago Tribune |date=November 1, 2011 |access-date=November 1, 2011 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20111102141236/http://www.chicagotribune.com/video/breaking/chi-video-was-kim-kardashian-marriage-divorce-a-sham-20111101%2C0%2C7143953.htmlstory |archive-date=November 2, 2011 }}</ref>

In April 2013, after a lengthy legal battle, Humphries and Kardashian reached a divorce settlement.<ref>{{cite news|title=Kris Humphries divorce agreed on|url=https://www.espn.com/new-york/nba/story/_/id/9189962/kim-kardashian-kris-humphries-agree-divorce-terms|work=ESPN.com|date=April 19, 2013|access-date=April 19, 2013}}</ref> Their divorce was finalized on June 3, 2013.<ref>{{cite news|title=Kim Kardashian and Kris Humphries finalize divorce|url=http://www.cbsnews.com/news/kim-kardashian-and-kris-humphries-finalize-divorce/|publisher=CBSNews.com|date=June 4, 2013|access-date=June 4, 2013}}</ref>
